structure: Part 13 read every file in src/server/app/shared/ in full (23 files, 2,913 lines): the page layout layout.njk and its test; kit.js (a JavaScript module of route options, chrome builders base/serverWideBase/chromeFor, the status strip, error summary and field error view models, the save-and-continue target, refusal, recoverable-save and stale-save handling, and the Ministry of Justice date field) and kit.test.js; the two Nunjucks macros saveActions (save-actions.njk) and sectionCaption (section-caption.njk) with their tests; the partials error.njk and error-summary.njk; trail.js (the from/return query markers and Back link) and its test; set-context.js (set mounts and per-set configuration) and its test; paths.js and paging.js; render-macro.js and its test; copy.js, copy.en.js, copy.cy.js, copy-leaves.js and copy.test.js. It covers the browser title, header, service navigation, phase banner, maturity banner, Back link, recoverable-error and stale-notification banners, status strip, content width and footer; every save control and where each goes; the error summary, field errors and error pages; the section caption; every English and Welsh shared copy key including the default validation messages; the URL shapes and paging rules (no page size is set here); and mechanism claims for the trail, the set context, macro rendering and copy-leaf checking, with what each test file holds them to. Claims 001-095 are kept from the earlier extract except 063, replaced by 096 to say the refusal log is only for refusals that are not the trader's own input.

claims.statement: The shared macro kit is the save controls and the section caption; there is no macro library beyond those two, and the rest of the shared kit is view-model building and route wiring rather than markup.
claims.quote: import { dashboardPath, hubPath, pagePath, pageRoutePath } from './paths.js'
claims.note: The part's covers expects "every macro in kit.js". kit.js is a JavaScript module and defines no Nunjucks macro: it exports route options and route pairs, the chrome builders base/serverWideBase/chromeFor, the status strip, the error summary and field error view models, the save-and-continue target, the refusal and recoverable-save logging and the Ministry of Justice date field. The only Nunjucks macros in src/server/app/shared/ are saveActions (save-actions.njk) and sectionCaption (section-caption.njk), and the two partials error.njk and error-summary.njk; all are claimed above.

claims.statement: Beyond the Ministry of Justice date picker, every shared component of the chrome is a GOV.UK Frontend one: back link, notification banner, phase banner, service navigation, tag, header, footer, button, button group, error summary.
claims.note: The only non-GOV.UK classes in the shared chrome are the house classes app-header, app-journey-strip and app-date-picker.

claims.statement: When a page refuses something that is not the trader's own correctable input (a state refusal, a tampered post, another service refusing), it logs one info line with the notification id, the route, the keys of any fields in error and any named reason or ids it turned on, never the messages the trader is shown.
claims.quote:
Only for a refusal that is not the user's own
 * input (a state refusal, a tampered post, another service refusing), never
 * for errors the user can correct on the form.
claims.note: Log message is 'Answer refused, page shown again'. kit.test.js:332-376 holds the field keys logged as errorCodes, extra ids such as addressId carried, and a named reason with empty errorCodes when the page shows no errors.

claims.statement: When saving opens the page that asks for a missing earlier answer instead of the next page, that detour is logged once at info with the notification id, the route, the page saved, the page opened and the ids of the missing answers.

claims.statement: A save refused because the notification changed since the page was shown is logged once at info with the notification id and the concurrency token the page posted, and the trader is redirected back to the same page with staleAction=1 added to whatever query string the URL already carried.

claims.note: kit.test.js:146-169 holds the redirect '/notifications/journey-1/origin?from=notification-view&staleAction=1' and the single log entry. Every page's POST route is wrapped this way by pageRoutes.

claims.statement: A save that fails because the notification is stale is not answered with the recoverable-error fallback: it is passed on to the stale-action handling, and any failure that is neither stale nor a recoverable backend error is passed on unlogged.
claims.note: mechanism: classifies the error a save throws. kit.test.js:299-329 holds both rethrows with no log line; kit.test.js:191-230 holds that the fallback warning carries the error only when it was not already logged where it was raised, plus any ids the page passes.
